title: Philippine Red Cross activated its typhoon Early Action Protocol on 510's machine-learning impact forecast before Storm Nalgae (October 2022)
summary: 510 ML impact forecast hit the trigger on 27 Oct 2022; PRC installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae
account: The Philippine Red Cross's Early Action Protocol for typhoons, approved in December 2019, uses an impact-based forecasting model developed with 510 (Netherlands Red Cross), which applies machine learning to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. On 27 October 2022, as Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached, the 510/IBF forecast projected shelter damage up to 10 percent in priority municipalities, reaching the trigger with 56 hours' lead time. Using IFRC anticipatory DREF funds, PRC activated the protocol in Aurora Province; between 27 and 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. PRC's post-storm survey reports all 78 kits installed and 390 people reached; CHF 7,002 of the CHF 117,555 budget was spent.
purpose: Forecast typhoon housing damage per municipality to trigger pre-agreed early actions before landfall.
system: 510 impact-based forecasting (IBF) model for typhoons in the Philippines, operated through the 510 dashboard with PAGASA forecasts
developer: 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross, with the Philippine Red Cross and German Red Cross
deployer: Philippine Red Cross, with IFRC anticipatory DREF funding
domain: Disaster risk reduction and forecast-based financing
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; shelter reinforcement before the storm reduces potential harm, but the post-storm survey gives no counterfactual.

ratings.reason: 78 households had roofs and walls reinforced before landfall; PRC reports they mitigated wind impact (implementer survey, no counterfactual).
First completed activation of the Philippine typhoon EAP; lessons on lead time and weather constraints documented in the final report.
Small scale: 390 people reached in one municipality.

ai_role.statement: The ML impact forecast was the trigger: under the EAP, early actions fire when the forecast wind impact on housing, 72 hours before landfall, is at least 10% of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities; the notification records the Aurora municipalities as 'Met (More than 10%)' with the 72-hour lead-time condition not met, and the final report says the 56-hour lead time was exceptionally granted. The notification states the projection came from the 510/IBF forecast incorporating PAGASA data. PRC staff confirmed chapter capacity and chose municipalities; the outcome claim is PRC's own post-storm survey. The NHESS paper and EGU abstract describing the model have 510 staff as co-authors, not lead authors.

headline: 510's ML forecast triggers PRC shelter kits before Storm Nalgae
metric: installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae

later.note: The IFRC final report of 30 June 2023 records all 78 households served and houses reinforced before impact, but a PRC lessons-learned workshop judged the trigger high and recommended reviewing the typhoon EAP.
later.quote: In addition, the trigger was considered high according to the solicited lessons from Paeng Lesson learned Workshop conducted by PRC with the support IFRC. Thus, one of the recommendations gathered is to review and revisit the Typhoon EAP.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 536 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Corrected the final report's date to its cover date of 30 June 2023 (18 January 2024 was the PDF file timestamp) and the notification's date to its launch date of 27 October 2022, marked the NHESS paper and EGU abstract independent because 510 staff are co-authors rather than lead authors, and restated the EAP trigger as at least 10% of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall, with the lead-time condition waived at 56 hours.
Benefit type set to Reduced Risk under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Added what happened since, the model version from the cited sources.

claim_basis: The makers' peer-reviewed study, the makers' other and two reports from the deployer are on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
